request: Goblin Chef (Rotgut Grenadier) (rotgut-grenadier): defeat animation from an owner-approved Runway reference video (front view, 6 s). refs/rotgut-grenadier--front.jpg is his model from the front; refs/rotgut-grenadier-death/frames/fall-over/f01..f12.jpg is part 1 (0-3 s) and refs/rotgut-grenadier-death/frames/lying-still/f01..f12.jpg is part 2 (3-6 s), 12 evenly spaced frames per part, time order. IGNORE in the video: the face, camera drift, and the small sideways shuffle of the feet at the very start (feet stay planted until he sits down). Owner rules for every goblin: nothing goes through his body, his held item or the ground; feet planted unless told otherwise (no sliding or sinking); weighty and cartoony, never floaty; poses read clearly from above and in front (board game camera). BASE POSE: these clips use "base_pose": "rest", so ctx.key turns are relative to the model's REST pose, the straight front-facing pose in refs/rotgut-grenadier--front.jpg. He faces straight forward (+Z, toward the camera) like the video. This is a rig motion reference only: never animate the face. FIRST Read all the pictures for a move, then match his BODY and LIMB poses frame by frame (torso lean and twist, head tilt, arm and leg angles, hip height) and the timing. If refs/ is missing or empty, do NOT write any animation files (the job will be retried). Do not touch, rename or remove any existing clip.

animations.name: OH_Death
animations.description: Death, from the owner-approved video: part 1 'fall-over' (refs/rotgut-grenadier-death/frames/fall-over, f01-f12) then part 2 'lying-still' (refs/rotgut-grenadier-death/frames/lying-still). Frames 0-75 follow fall-over f01-f12 (frame N of 12 = about N*6 frames): from the base pose he wobbles as if very dizzy (small sway of hips and spine, head lolls), knees buckle, he sits straight down onto his bottom on the spot (about f09-f10), then tips gently backwards onto his back (f11-f12), legs up a little then down. Frames 75-90 he settles flat on his back like lying-still f01-f04 (small bounce, arms fall loosely out to the sides, legs relax). Frames 90-120 he lies completely still in that pose (no breathing). Use "move" on the hips to lower him to the floor: the hips go straight DOWN (and slightly back) only to the heights given below, so his body rests ON the floor, never under it. He stays in his own square: no sliding, no rolling away; his hips end within about 15% of his height of where they started. He keeps holding his big spatula the whole time (it stays in his hand and lies flat on the floor beside him at the end, never through the floor). This clip does NOT return to idle: key every bone you use at the last frame (120) with the lying pose so the clip ends lying down. LYING POSE: lay him FLAT on his back: hips turned back about 85-90 degrees, spine and chest nearly in line with the hips, legs lying out in front, arms resting on the floor at his sides, spatula flat on the floor beside him. MEASURED ON YOUR LAST TRY (rotgut-grenadier-runway-death-r2, frame 120): the joint heights were fine, but the MESH is thick around them, so skin went up to 15% of his height under the floor (his tall CHEF HAT through the floor behind his head, and his boots). When he lies, the skin reaches this far BELOW each joint (share of ctx.height): Head with the chef hat 23%, Spine02/Spine01 10%, shoulders 6-8%, upper arms 6-13%, forearms and hands 5-6%, thighs (UpLeg) 18%, shins (Leg, with the boots) 23%, feet 4-6%. So in the lying pose (frames 77-120) put EVERY joint at least that high above the floor plus 1%: hips about 0.19 x height, spine joints about 0.11, shoulders about 0.09, hands about 0.07, knees about 0.24, ankles about 0.24 (lower legs resting with the boots on their heels, toes up). HEAD AND HAT: tilt his head forward, chin toward his chest (about 30-40 degrees), so the tall hat lies along the floor behind his head instead of pointing down into it; keep the head joint about 0.15-0.2 x height above the floor. Same idea for the sit-down (frames 50-65): his bottom and thighs sit ON the floor, hips about 0.19 x height. Nothing may go under the floor at any frame.
